next_question: On a substrate that satisfies a preregistered surface contract and supplies at least 150 never-observed identifiers per family across at least two structurally different resource shapes, can a mechanism induced from observations of TWO structurally different resources -- with no hand-declared identity slot and no hand-supplied prefix rule -- learn which path segments are variable, and then transfer to a never-observed THIRD resource whose URL shape matches neither training resource, at task success >= 0.95 measured as verb AND status AND returned entity, and at amortized_cost_ratio <= 0.85 against an executed per-task cold-discovery baseline, with a mandatory null arm that induces from a single resource and is required to PIN (success <= 0.10) so that the test discriminates variability-observation from template-construction skill rather than reproducing the pinned-treatment result of this packet?
why_next: This packet is the first in the program to produce a real transfer measurement and the first to produce a genuinely executed cold-discovery comparator, and together they localize the missing ingredient precisely instead of leaving it diffuse. The prereg-named Treatment pinned the collection and scored 0.0000 on 126 never-observed resource-B identifiers; the identical pipeline scored 1.0000 CI [1.0000,1.0000] on those same identifiers once the collection was induced as a declared identity slot; and the auditor supplies the mechanism: all 50 induction identifiers live in one collection, so the collection segment is constant across the entire training set, and a segment that never varies carries no evidence that it should vary. That is a statement about what induction can know, not about how a template is built, so the next question must change the INDUCTION INPUT rather than re-run the template builder -- otherwise it repeats this packet inside the same solution basin. Declaring the varying segment by hand is what made the last positive work, and a hand-declared slot cannot be the answer for an agent that has never seen the resource, so the next experiment must ask whether variability can be LEARNED from a second structurally different resource and then applied to a third whose shape matches neither. That design also gives the experiment its null for free: single-resource induction is the known pinning failure and must reproduce, so the test discriminates variability-observation from template-construction skill instead of re-deriving the same result. Three further reasons this is the right next question rather than a repeat or a pivot. Re-running the current design is not informative because its gate was undecidable for reasons no amount of re-execution touches: F2 cannot be satisfied on a substrate with no /api/v1 prefix and contradicts T1, F6 is an algebraic identity that cannot fire at any data, F9 penalises correct abstention at zero requests, and F12 failed at 42 per family because the substrate exposes only 126 resource-B identifiers. The next question is therefore written to require a substrate that satisfies a preregistered surface contract and supplies at least 150 identifiers per family, so a digest match can no longer stand in for design validation. It also forbids a hand-declared slot, so it cannot be won by declaration again. And pivoting away from inheritance would discard the only mechanism in the program that has now been shown to transfer across a resource boundary, which would be a false economy: the domain is not exhausted, this one bounded design was. The honest summary of the cycle is that inheritance now has a demonstrated transfer result and an identified missing ingredient, and the highest-information move is to test whether that ingredient can be learned rather than supplied.

established: Bounded mechanism result, prereg-named arm, verified by the Director against the audit's recomputation (all matches_producer true): induction from a SINGLE-collection training set pins the collection segment and cannot transfer to a second resource. The prereg-named Treatment bound /items/PROD-100 style paths and achieved task success 0.0000, CI [0.0000,0.0000], on all 126 never-observed resource-B identifiers (42 per family), with HTTP-level success also 0.0000. It emitted well-formed, prefix-preserved requests. The diagnosed structural cause, from audit.validity_findings and result.json.validity_notes: all 50 induction identifiers live in the 'items' collection, so the collection segment is constant across the whole training set and therefore carries no evidence that it should vary. This is a property of the training distribution, NOT evidence that prefix preservation is wrong.

Bounded mechanism result, added DIAGNOSTIC arm, not preregistered and must be labelled as such wherever it is cited: with the resource collection induced as a DECLARED identity slot, template /${collection}/${id}, the SAME pipeline reaches task success 1.0000, CI [1.0000,1.0000], on those same 126 never-observed resource-B identifiers at 1.0159 requests per task. The producer labelled it added_diagnostic_treatment_identity_slot_success_rate; the audit recomputed it independently as treatment_identity_slot_success_rate.

The transfer result above is not identifier leakage. The substrate exposes 200 resource-A identifiers: indices 0-149 are the PC-SAME-RESOURCE held-out set at 50 per family and indices 150-199 are the induction training set of 50 distinct identifiers reused across the three families to produce 150 observations. The held-out set is index-disjoint from the training set, and the resource-A and resource-B identifier namespaces are disjoint by construction (200 versus 126, empty intersection).

First genuinely EXECUTED cold-discovery comparator in the program, and therefore the first amortization denominator with real dynamic range: B-COLD achieved mean 4.079365079365079 requests per task, CI [4.015873015873016, 4.158730158730159] with family-stratified B=5000 bootstrap, task success 1.0000, on 126 tasks measured per task rather than configured. The run issued 1746 counted HTTP requests in total, of which 14 were charged re-authentications forced by the substrate's TOKEN_EXPIRY=100 with no issuance endpoint. Induction cost 152 was counted by the client, not estimated as len(observations)*15.

Against that executed B-COLD the identity-slot mechanism reaches an amortized cost ratio of 0.5447470817120622, below the 0.85 threshold, with break-even at 50 transfer tasks and 126 executed, so it is past break-even. This is the first program result where the amortization denominator is a measurement.

The min_confidence gate is load-bearing for safety, and this is the strongest datum in the packet. NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT abstained on 126/126 tasks at zero requests, with induced confidences 0.38, 0.40 and 0.44 against an 0.8 execution threshold, transfer_success 0.0000 and abstention_precision 1.0000 over 60 negative probes. With the gate bypassed (NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT-FORCED) the same mechanisms returned HTTP 200 on 100 percent of tasks, applied the WRONG VERB on 84 of 126, and accomplished the task on 0.3333. This independently reproduces the parent packet's 80-wrong-action liability estimate on a substrate built independently of the parent's.

The positive control works through the shipped-kernel path rather than by hand-building a Mechanism: PC-SAME-RESOURCE reached success 1.0000, CI [1.0000,1.0000], on n=150 at 50 per family through distill_parameterized, with induced template /items/${id} and prefix preservation true. tests/test_kernel.py carries 10 tests, all reaching EXECUTABLE through distill_parameterized rather than inserting a Mechanism at confidence 0.95, and the suite reports OK with 0 failures.

rejected: Bounded to this run: reading the prereg-named Treatment's 0.0000 as evidence that prefix-preserving parameter induction cannot transfer across resources, or that the inheritance architecture is not viable. The record of 0.0000 stands and must not be erased; the inference is rejected because the structural cause is identified (a single-collection training set gives no evidence that the collection segment should vary) and the same pipeline transfers at 1.0000 when the variable segment is declared. This is the same bounded reading the parent handoff applied to its own non-discriminating thresholds.

Bounded to this run: reading the pinned Treatment's 0.0000 as evidence that prefix PRESERVATION is wrong or unnecessary. Rejected on the audit's own structural analysis, which cuts the other way -- prereg section 5.1's prefix-preservation requirement is insufficient on its own to obtain transfer, but nothing here shows it is harmful.

Bounded to this run: falsifier clauses F2, F6 and F9 as instruments, in either direction. F2 requires a bound path of the form /api/v1/<collection>/<slot> on a substrate that serves no /api/v1 prefix, and it contradicts prereg T1 at prereg.md:93, which pins action_template.path to /api/v1/items/${id}, so the two clauses are mutually unsatisfiable as written. F6 compares break_even_transfer_tasks against N_MAX, where N_MAX = ceil(induction_cost/(mean_bcold - treatment_cost)) is the same algebraic expression as break-even, verified numerically at 50 == 50, so the clause is an identity that cannot fire at any data; n_max_frozen was also never written to spec.json or freeze.json as prereg section 8.4 requires. F9 requires the null arm's cost ratio against B-COLD to be at least 1.0, which a correctly abstaining arm issuing zero requests can never satisfy, so the threshold penalises correct abstention. These are design defects, not findings about inheritance.

Bounded to this run: the 2.1875 ratio against B-LITERAL-REPLAY and the 0.9722 ratio against B-RETRIEVAL-K5 as economic evidence, in either direction. Neither baseline is a comparator. B-LITERAL-REPLAY returns HTTP 200 on 126/126 tasks while accomplishing 0 of them, at 1.0159 requests per task, which is cheaper than the treatment, because it silently acts on the wrong entity (GET /items/PROD-100 returns 200 with items data, not products data). B-RETRIEVAL-K5 scores task success 0.0000 under a disclosed substitution of a deterministic hashed character-n-gram bag for semantic embeddings, no model key or embedding service being available. Decision-rule condition 5 therefore requires a win 'at matched end-to-end success' against two arms that score 0.0, and the comparison has no referent.

Bounded to this run: reading the null arm's abstention_precision 1.0000 as evidence that the kernel is safe. The gate guards INTENT, not slot values. The identity-slot treatment arms accepted 20 of 20 out-of-support identifier bindings and 10 of 20 empty-string bindings, and rejected 20 of 20 invalid intents, giving false_accept_rate 0.5 and abstention_precision 0.5 for the treatment arms. A product kernel would act on any string in any slot.

Bounded to this run: ece_treatment 0.0 as calibration evidence. Every task resolves through one mechanism at one confidence value, so the expected calibration error is structurally 0.0 with n_bins_effective 1 and carries no calibration information. Related: the derived confidence value can reach exactly 1.0 on this deterministic substrate because support and template consistency are both 100 percent, so the substrate cannot exercise the low-confidence regime at all.

Bounded to this run: the F12 sample-size failure as evidence about inheritance. Every resource-B arm reached 42 per family rather than the preregistered 50, because the frozen substrate exposes 126 resource-B identifiers, which cannot supply 150. This is a substrate capacity limit. Compounding it, the family-stratified B=5000 bootstrap intervals are degenerate at 0.0 or 1.0 wherever every resampled task shares one outcome, which is frequent at n=42, so no per-family margin may be quoted from this packet.

Bounded to this run: the frozen gate as a source of any scientific inference. result.json.decision_rule_evaluation.gate_result is NOT_DECIDABLE_AS_FROZEN, and it fails for three reasons that must never be pooled into one number: one genuine mechanism result (Treatment 0.0000), three clauses that cannot discriminate as written (F2, F6, F9), and one substrate capacity shortfall (F12). The verdict neither reports the conjunction as FALSIFIES, which would convert design and infrastructure defects into a scientific negative, nor as SUPPORTS, which would convert a post-hoc added diagnostic arm into a passed gate.

Whether variability can be LEARNED rather than DECLARED. The packet's structural law -- a segment that never varies across the training set carries no evidence that it should vary -- is inferred from a single-collection training set and is stated as an explanation, not tested. Whether induction over two structurally different resources discovers which segments are variable, and then applies that to a third resource of neither shape, is the open question this handoff proposes.

Whether the identity-slot result generalizes at all beyond this substrate. Nothing here speaks to real Web APIs, real sites, browser interaction, cross-site transfer, model-based or semantic resolution, model tokens, latency, token cost, or any surface with genuinely different URL shapes. The substrate offers two collections and four item-level verbs, so the three families differ by VERB and intent namespace only; all three share the path form /{collection}/{id}.

Whether a sound baseline can be given a non-zero success rate, which is the precondition for 'matched end-to-end success' to mean anything. Both non-cold baselines scored 0.0. Whether B-RETRIEVAL-K5 discriminates with a real semantic embedding is untested, and whether any literal-replay or retrieval comparator can succeed on a resource whose URL shape differs from the induced one is unknown.
